title: Parahoric Action on the Generalized Lattice Model
body_html:
Parahoric Action on the Generalized Lattice Model

Let \(x\in\mathcal B(\operatorname{Sp}(W))\), with generalized lattice model \(\Omega_x=S(\mathscr L_{x,0})\) of functions \(f:W\to S(\mathsf b_x)\) satisfying \[ f(a+w)=\psi\!\big(\tfrac12\langle w,a\rangle\big)\,\overline{\omega}_x(\bar a)\,f(w),\qquad a\in\mathscr L_{x,0}, \] where \(\mathsf b_x=\mathscr L_{x,0}/\mathscr L_{x,0+}\) and \(\overline{\omega}_x\) is the oscillator representation of the finite Heisenberg group \(H(\mathsf b_x)\) and of \(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathsf b_x)\) (see Generalized Lattice Model, Symplectic Weil Representation over a Finite Field). The parahoric \(G_{x,0}\) stabilizes \(\mathscr L_{x,0}\) and \(\mathscr L_{x,0+}\), hence reduces to \(\bar g\in\operatorname{Sp}(\mathsf b_x)\) under \(G_{x,0}\to\operatorname{Sp}(\mathsf b_x)\) (see Parahoric Reductive Quotient for Sp(W)).

The action

\(G_{x,0}\) acts on \(\Omega_x\) by the natural translation, twisted by the finite Weil action on the values: \[ \boxed{\;(\omega_x(g)f)(w)=\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)\,f(g^{-1}w),\qquad g\in G_{x,0},\ f\in\Omega_x,\ w\in W.\;} \] This is the default action of \(G_{x,0}\) on \(\Omega_x\), written \(\omega_x\); here \(\overline{\omega}_x\) denotes the finite Weil representation \(\omega_{\mathsf b_x}\) of \(\mathsf b_x\). The factor \(f\mapsto f\circ g^{-1}\) is the geometric action of \(g\in\operatorname{Sp}(W)\) on functions on \(W\) (no Jacobian, since \(g\) preserves the symplectic form and the lattice); \(\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)\) is the finite Weil action on the coefficient space \(S(\mathsf b_x)\).

This \(\omega_x\) is a genuine representation of \(G_{x,0}\) (no central extension needed, because over a residue field of odd order the finite Weil representation \(\overline{\omega}_x\) is a true representation of \(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathsf b_x)\)). Equivalently it is the lattice-model splitting \[ \xi_x:G_{x,0}\to Mp(W),\qquad \omega_x=\omega_\psi\circ\xi_x , \] the \(\xi_B\) of Generalized Lattice Model specialized to the point \(x\). It is canonical: the only datum is the additive character \(\psi\); no polarization, comparison intertwiner, or Haar choice enters.

On the pro-unipotent radical \(G_{x,0+}\) the reduction is trivial (\(\bar g=1\)), so \[ (\omega_x(g)f)(w)=f(g^{-1}w),\qquad g\in G_{x,0+}, \] pure translation — which is why the splitting is canonical on \(G_{x,0+}\); the genuine content of \(\xi_x\) lives on the finite reductive quotient \(\mathsf G_x\), through \(\overline{\omega}_x\).
proof_html:
Well-defined. For \(a\in\mathscr L_{x,0}\), \(g^{-1}a\in\mathscr L_{x,0}\) and \(\langle g^{-1}w,g^{-1}a\rangle=\langle w,a\rangle\), so the covariance gives \[ (\omega_x(g)f)(a+w)=\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)\,f(g^{-1}a+g^{-1}w) =\psi\!\big(\tfrac12\langle w,a\rangle\big)\,\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)\,\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g^{-1}\bar a)\,f(g^{-1}w). \] The intertwining property of the oscillator representation, \(\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)\,\overline{\omega}_x(\bar v)\,\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)^{-1}=\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g\bar v)\) for \(\bar v\in\mathsf b_x\), turns \(\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g^{-1}\bar a)\) into \(\overline{\omega}_x(\bar a)\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g)\), so \((\omega_x(g)f)(a+w)=\psi(\tfrac12\langle w,a\rangle)\,\overline{\omega}_x(\bar a)\,(\omega_x(g)f)(w)\); hence \(\omega_x(g)f\in\Omega_x\).

Multiplicative. \((\omega_x(g_1)\omega_x(g_2)f)(w)=\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g_1)\overline{\omega}_x(\bar g_2)f((g_1g_2)^{-1}w) =\overline{\omega}_x(\overline{g_1g_2})f((g_1g_2)^{-1}w)=(\omega_x(g_1g_2)f)(w)\), using that \(\bar{\cdot}\) is a homomorphism and \(\overline{\omega}_x\) a representation of \(\operatorname{Sp}(\mathsf b_x)\). The identification \(\omega_x=\omega_\psi\circ\xi_x\) is the lattice-model construction of Generalized Lattice Model. \(\square\)
